newsitem.title: USA: High-yield U.S. mutual funds see cash inflows drop.
newsitem.headline: High-yield U.S. mutual funds see cash inflows drop.

text.p: Cash inflows into high-yield mutual funds dropped dramatically over the past week, but defied market expectations by remaining net positive, market sources said.
Net flows into high-yield mutual funds dropped to $152 million this week from $527 million in the prior week, according to AMG Data Service, market sources said.

"While it is a positive number, it is much weaker than previous weeks," said Sam DeRosa-Farag, head of high-yield strategy at Chase Securities Inc. "Still, it is really not as weak as our expectations."
Mutual fund redemptions, particularly by "market timer" investors, were believed to be a major factor behind a roughly 0.5 percent drop in high-yield bond prices this week.
Junk market players said comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan that the high-yield market may be overvalued rattled the confidence of investors.
DeRosa-Farag said this week's positive numbers suggested mutual fund flows and negative sentiment were less significant.
AMG, based in Arcata, California, is a U.S. mutual fund information company.
As of Friday morning, when the numbers were released, traders said high-yield prices were unchanged from yesterday's closing levels.
